subtitle: Master reverb effects to create depth, space, and atmosphere in your guitar sounds

introduction.title: Understanding Reverb
introduction.text: Reverb is one of the most fundamental effects in music production, simulating the natural acoustic reflections that occur in physical spaces. It adds depth, dimension, and atmosphere to your guitar sound, transforming a dry signal into something that feels alive and situated in a real or imagined space.
introduction.quote: Reverb doesn't just add space—it creates the emotional context for your music, whether that's the intimate closeness of a small room or the grandeur of a cathedral.

cards.title: Room Reverb
cards.description: Short decay time (0.3-1.2 seconds), clear defined reflections, natural intimate sound, preserves note definition

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Short decay time (0.3-1.2 seconds), clear defined reflections, natural intimate sound, preserves note definition

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Country and folk guitar, jazz comping, blues rhythm parts, acoustic guitar simulation

cards.title: Hall Reverb
cards.description: Long decay time (2-8 seconds), smooth diffuse reflections, grand spacious sound, rich harmonic content

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Long decay time (2-8 seconds), smooth diffuse reflections, grand spacious sound, rich harmonic content

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Ambient and post-rock, ballad solos, classical crossover, cinematic soundscapes

cards.title: Spring Reverb
cards.description: Distinctive "boing" character, medium decay with metallic overtones, vintage analog warmth

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Distinctive "boing" character, medium decay with metallic overtones, vintage analog warmth, crash sensitivity (dramatic effect when hit)

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Surf rock, vintage country, rockabilly, classic rock rhythm

cards.title: Plate Reverb
cards.description: Bright shimmering quality, fast initial buildup, dense metallic character, classic studio sound

fields.label: Characteristics
fields.value: Bright shimmering quality, fast initial buildup, dense metallic character, classic studio sound

fields.label: Musical Applications
fields.value: Classic rock leads, vocal-style guitar lines, 60s and 70s recordings, studio productions

cards.title: Decay Time
cards.description: How long the reverb takes to fade away
items: Short (0.3-1s): Intimate, controlled
Medium (1-3s): Natural, musical
Long (3-8s): Dramatic, atmospheric

cards.title: Room Size
cards.description: The perceived size of the simulated space
items: Small: Tight, present sound
Medium: Balanced, natural
Large: Spacious, enveloping

cards.title: Pre-delay
cards.description: Time between dry signal and reverb onset
items: 0-10ms: Immediate, ambient
10-30ms: Natural separation
30ms+: Distinct echo effect

cards.title: Mix/Wet Level
cards.description: Balance between dry and reverb signal
items: 10-20%: Subtle enhancement
20-40%: Noticeable ambience
40%+: Atmospheric, dreamy

cards.title: "In the Air Tonight" - Phil Collins
cards.description: Gated reverb on drums, but the guitar uses subtle hall reverb

fields.label: Settings
fields.value: Hall reverb, medium size, 2-3 second decay, 25% mix level, high-frequency damping

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates atmospheric tension, supports the song's drama, complements the iconic drum sound, maintains clarity in the mix

fields.label: Settings
fields.value: Fender-style spring reverb, high reverb level (6-8), fast attack medium decay, bright splashy character

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Defines the surf rock genre, creates oceanic imagery, adds excitement and energy, vintage amp authenticity

cards.title: "Shine On You Crazy Diamond" - Pink Floyd
cards.description: Long, lush hall reverb on lead guitar

fields.label: Settings
fields.value: Large hall reverb, 4-6 second decay, 40-50% mix level, smooth diffuse character

fields.label: Musical Effect
fields.value: Creates vast cosmic atmosphere, supports emotional expression, blends notes into sustained textures, enhances the song's epic scope

fields.label: Chord Voicings
fields.value: Open voicings work better with reverb than dense, closed chords. The space allows reverb to enhance rather than muddy the sound.

fields.label: Note Sustain
fields.value: Let notes ring and overlap slightly with reverb. This creates beautiful harmonic interactions and natural flow.

fields.label: Dynamic Control
fields.value: Use your picking dynamics to control reverb perception. Softer playing makes reverb more prominent in the mix.

fields.label: Frequency Balance
fields.value: Use high-cut filters on reverb returns to prevent harsh reflections. Low-cut prevents muddy buildup.

fields.label: Stereo Imaging
fields.value: Wide stereo reverbs create space, while mono reverbs add depth without width. Match to your song's needs.

fields.label: Send vs. Insert
fields.value: Use reverb as a send effect when possible to maintain mix clarity and create cohesive spatial imaging.

cards.title: What to Avoid
items: Too much reverb overwhelming the dry signal
Using long reverbs on fast, intricate passages
Ignoring the song's tempo and mood
Same reverb setting for all guitar parts
Not considering other instruments in the mix

cards.title: Best Practices
items: Start with subtle settings and build up
Match reverb to the song's emotional content
Use pre-delay to maintain note definition
EQ your reverb to fit the mix
Consider the vocalist's reverb for cohesion

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Room Size Comparison
items: Play the same chord progression (try Em - C - G - D) with three different reverb settings
Small room, short decay (intimate coffee shop)
Medium hall, moderate decay (concert hall)
Large hall, long decay (cathedral)
Notice how each setting changes the emotional impact and suggests different musical contexts

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Genre Matching
items: Country: Short room reverb, bright character
Surf rock: Spring reverb, high mix level
Ambient: Long hall reverb, atmospheric
Blues: Subtle room reverb, natural feel

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Dynamic Reverb
items: Set a moderate reverb level
Play at full volume, then roll back to create swells
Notice how reverb becomes more prominent at lower volumes
Practice creating ambient textures between chord changes
